messages:
alex: Heads-up — I flipped on FP8 transformer-engine kernels on the H100 validation cluster and hit two things: overall throughput drops ~15% on long-context (8k+) runs and we're seeing sporadic NaNs in the KV-cache heavy traces. attaching quick profiler output in a sec.

ryan: ugh. which TE version and flags? any kernel overrides?

alex: TE v1.11 build, flags: `TE_FP8=true TE_FP8_MODE=e4m3 TE_ENABLE_KV_OPT=1`. config snippet:
```
transformer_engine:
  version: 1.11
  fp8:
    enabled: true
    format: e4m3
    clip_factor: 0.7
  kv_opt: true
  kernel_preference: autoselect
```

perf-bot: microbench summary: baseline (fp16 matmul + int8 ffn): p50=45ms p95=180ms throughput=120 req/s. fp8-on-h100: p50=52ms p95=210ms throughput=100 req/s. regression ~16.7% throughput, p95 tail +16%.

lina: Are NaNs reproducible? small repro script? Also try disabling KV cache to isolate — could be fp8 scaling mismatch in KV write path.

alex: NaNs are semi-deterministic on our long chat trace set. Disabled KV cache (`use_kv_cache=false`) — NaNs disappeared, but throughput got worse (p50->58ms). So looks like KV path + FP8 interaction.

maria: interesting. Could be per-layer calibration drift on KV write/restore. Did we run layerwise calibration? default was global calibration during load. Try per-layer `--per-layer-calib` and increase iters.

alex: ran `calibrate_layers.py --mode=histogram --iters=300 --per-layer-calib` — quality stable, but perf stayed lower. Also noticed kernel selector picks TE matmul FP8 kernels but falls back to a generic slow path for fused attention on larger seq lengths. profiling snippet:
```
[PROFILE] attention_forward: selected_kernel=te_fp8_attn_v2 (fallback_count=423)
[PROFILE] ffn_matmul: selected_kernel=te_fp8_gemm (fast)
[PROFILE] kv_write: selected_kernel=generic_fp16_write (slow, 1.6x)
```

ryan: fallback_count=423 is huge. kernel autoselect is probably hitting heuristics that favor correctness for long seqs. We can try forcing kernel override for attention to `te_fp8_attn_v1` or force TE to prefer fp16 for attention. Also check TE build flags for `KV_FP8_SUPPORT` — maybe only partial.

lina: on L40S we saw different behavior — TE chooses a different attention kernel that was faster. Could be driver differences. Can you run a quick compare: H100 vs L40S with same trace and kernsel logs?

alex: did that — L40S throughput was actually better with FP8 (p50 48ms) and fewer fallbacks. So hardware/driver kernel availability seems to matter.

maria: for NaNs: try setting `fp8_clip=1.0` (increase clip) and `TE_FP8_USE_FP16_BACKUP=1` so if FP8 op yields NaN it falls back to FP16. That should stop correctness issues while we debug perf.

alex: tried `TE_FP8_USE_FP16_BACKUP=1` — NaNs gone, perf slightly improved but still behind baseline. With backup enabled, fallback_count for attention dropped to ~80.

ryan: action plan: 1) open TE bug with kernel selector heuristics (attach kernsel logs + fallback counts), 2) add per-layer calibration into onboarding for FP8, 3) experiment with kernel overrides: force fp16-attn + fp8-ffn, 4) run the same on L40S and collect driver/kernel list.

alex: created issue RDW-OPS/te-kernsel-148 with logs and microbench table. Also pushed a short-term runtime change to prefer fp16-attn on H100 when seq_len>2048. Patch PR: `runtime: prefer_fp16_attn_on_long_context` (will A/B for a day).

lina: good. let's also flag the perf regression in the release notes and revert to int8 ffns for safety if SLA breaches.

maria: TL;DR: FP8 is promising on L40S but H100 currently needs kernsel + kv-path fixes; use `TE_FP8_USE_FP16_BACKUP=1` + per-layer calibration as interim.

alex: thanks — re-running long-context nightly suite with backup enabled and kernel override. I'll post results tomorrow. :thumbsup:
